Lesson overview:
- Level: A1 General English
- Unit: MODULE 3. OBJECTS & PERSONAL SPACE
- Time: 60 min (Essential) / 90 min (Expanded) / 120 min (Full Workshop)
- Focus: What's in Your Fridge
- Materials: vocabulary cards, audio, reading handout
Warm-up: say one word you already know for this topic.
Recycles there is / there are from Lesson 1.13.
Recycled language: milk, bread, cheese.
Answer from memory: which word belongs to this topic?
Which word belongs to this topic?
Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

milk — a white drink from cows. Example: There is some milk in the fridge.
bread — a baked food made from flour. Example: We need some bread.
cheese — a food made from milk. Example: There is some cheese on the plate.
butter — a yellow fat made from milk. Example: Put some butter on the bread.
egg — a food from a hen. Example: There are six eggs.
fruit — sweet food from a plant, like apples. Example: We have got some fruit.
vegetable — a plant food, like a carrot. Example: Eat a vegetable every day.
water — the clear liquid we drink. Example: There is some water in the glass.
fridge — a cold cupboard for food. Example: The milk is in the fridge.
shopping list — a list of things to buy. Example: Write a shopping list, please.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• There is some ...
• There isn't any ...
• Have we got any ...?
• Let's write a shopping list.
• We need ...
Vocabulary practice: choose the correct word.
Which word means 'a white drink from cows'?
Which word means 'a baked food made from flour'?
Complete the sentence with a word from the list.

some_of the milk, some_of the cheese
Listen and repeat three times.
Which word carries the main stress?
Grammar focus: Countable and uncountable nouns.
Countable nouns take a/an and plurals: an egg, two eggs. Uncountable nouns have no plural: milk, bread, water. Use some in statements and any in questions and negatives.
Controlled practice: choose the correct option.
Choose the correct sentence.
Choose the correct question.
Complete the sentence.
Reading: read the text and answer the questions.
There is some milk and some cheese in the fridge. There are six eggs and some fruit. There isn't any bread, so I need a shopping list.
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.
A: Have we got any milk? B: Yes, there is some. A: And any eggs? B: There are four eggs, but there isn't any bread.
Speaking: Pair and group tasks: Compare two fridges and write a shopping list.

• There is some ...
• There isn't any ...
• Have we got any ...?
Writing: Write four to five sentences about "Whats in Your Fridge" using the target grammar.
